extracted.intended_audience: MacRumors readers; general tech-news audience and PR/marketing/advertising professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating a corporate advertising spot and the appropriate corporate response when it offends audiences; covers creative choices, cultural sensitivity, messaging clarity, and corrective actions (apologies/removal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid depicting destruction of creative tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads should not portray creative tools or creative activity being destroyed, as that can be read as devaluing human creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Crush ad showed a hydraulic press crushing musical instruments, electronic equipment, arcade games, paint and brushes, computers, cameras, and more; critics called it the "destruction of the human experience" and said it "symbolizes everything everyone has ever hated about digitization." Avoid such imagery that suggests erasing or replacing creative labor or the tools creatives value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the room / cultural sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Creators and brands should assess current cultural sentiment and audience sensitivities before releasing provocative imagery or metaphors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director Reed Morano told Apple to "read the room" and called the spot "actually psychotic." The page implies that failing to account for how creatives and the broader public will interpret an ad can lead to backlash; brands should anticipate interpretations and possible offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure messaging doesn't overshadow intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual metaphors or stunts must clearly support — and not obscure or contradict — the intended product message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple intended to show the iPad as condensing many tools into a single device, but the 'crushing' imagery was perceived as harmful. Test whether dramatic imagery might distract from or negate the product's claimed benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cultural/viral references requires care
rubrics_metrics.description: Leveraging popular internet formats or viral trends (e.g., hydraulic press videos) is acceptable but risks misinterpretation if the reference clashes with brand values or audience expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ad was a play on popular hydraulic press videos; while trendy references can increase shareability, they must be evaluated for tone and potential negative connotations among key communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize celebrating and empowering target communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Brand messaging should celebrate the people who use the product and emphasize empowerment rather than replacing or diminishing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple's apology emphasized: "Creativity is in our DNA... design products that empower creatives all over the world... always celebrate the myriad of ways users express themselves." Ads should align with that approach rather than portraying creators as obsolete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate corrective action and transparency after backlash
rubrics_metrics.description: When an ad causes significant negative reaction, companies should acknowledge the misstep, apologize, and adjust distribution or placement as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple issued a statement saying the video "missed the mark" and apologized; the company left the video on YouTube but said the ad "won't be running on television." Effective responses contain acknowledgement, expression of regret, and concrete remedial steps (e.g., pulling TV buys).

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful channel and placement decisions for controversial content
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide distribution channels based on potential reach and risk; limit placement on broader channels if content may provoke broader public backlash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple chose to leave the Crush video on its YouTube channel but not run it on television, illustrating a tactic of containing contentious material to narrower or owned channels while avoiding mass-broadcast exposure.
